answer: To earn storage fees, an agent offering to mirror a canyon survey archive must prove it holds a replica at dawn. Encode each 10 GB replica with its public key using a slow sequential encoding; unpredictable block challenges have deadlines too short to regenerate missing blocks. Validators check the encoding against the archive and verify sampled Merkle proofs. Ten aliases need ten distinct replicas and timely reads, multiplying disk and bandwidth costs. Pay per verified replica, with no per-account bonus, so extra names alone earn nothing.
